name: Le Sirenuse
tagline: Fifty-eight rooms above Positano, with La Sponda and a spa.
description:
Le Sirenuse is a hotel in Positano, at Via Cristoforo Colombo 30, 84017 Positano. The house counts 58 rooms, from courtyard rooms to sea-view suites, and breakfast is included. Children up to six years old are not allowed, because of the stairs and balconies, and pets are not allowed. Check-in is at 15:00 and check-out at 12:00. The hotel is not an adults-only house. It simply does not take children under six.

Franco Sersale's antiques and ceramics from Salerno run through the rooms, and the bathroom line Eau d'Italie was born at the hotel. The Two Bedroom Suite Sea View measures about 110 square metres, with a terrace from 27 square metres, a sea-facing bath and a second bedroom. The house looks over Positano, the sea and the Li Galli islands.

Dinner is at La Sponda, open seven nights, with executive chef Gennaro Russo. The room is set with candles, and the musicians Franco and Andrea play. The pool sits among lemon trees and bougainvillea, with white loungers and a pool bar. The bar will do a spritz, a club sandwich or pasta al pomodoro made with tomatoes from the slopes of Mount Vesuvius. The gym has TechnoGym machines and two Megaformers. A coach also takes hikes on the old paths behind the town, and the hotel runs a Dolce Vitality fitness retreat twice a year.

The spa, designed by Gae Aulenti, has a sauna, a granite steam bath and an ice room with a ground ice cascade and backlit onyx. A Spa Suite is kept for couples. Treatments use Augustinus Bader, Aveda and Margy's Monte Carlo. Franco Sersale's photographs from his travels in the East hang in the spa.

Positano is 55 km south of Naples. The hotel gives the drive from Naples Capodichino Airport as typically 75 to 90 minutes. The telephone is +39 089 875066 and the email is info@sirenuse.it. The house suits a stay in the town itself, with dinner at La Sponda and the pool a few steps from the room.
